prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Dispatch Center (Juniper): intake/triage/dispatch; preserve reports/uncertainty, authorization/selection rationale; reconcile location/destination via Caller Location Correction Slip; verify Battery Swap Voucher readiness; use North Approach Queue Snapshot for routing; record approved alternatives/check coverage; evaluate destinations against acuity/time/coverage; produce Unit Staging Change Card. Call Taker Mara (Larkspur): verify/repeat location before medical details; capture callback/patient/symptom/hazard/access/source data; produce correction slip; confirm incident/intended facility before destination transmission. Triage Supervisor (Copperfield): prioritize/reassess threats/delay-harm; resolve disagreements/document rationale; confirm level; send Pediatric Acuity Note; advise demand-driven repositioning. Regional Medical Director: policy/delegation, elevated-demand priorities, specialized-capability/protocol destination guidance; no dispatch authority. Data Quality Officer: audit defects/rationale; route location/status corrections operationally; no independent clinical-priority changes. Ambulance Coordination Platform: consolidate incidents/assignments/positions/readiness/capabilities/coverage/access; retain timestamped status changes; present approved destinations/instructions. Computer Aided Dispatch Console: current authorized operational information; staff verify currency. Dispatcher: select by priority/needs/time/capability/readiness/coverage under authorization rules; compare projected response times/remaining coverage before moves; retransmit discrepancies/constraints/uncertainty. Shift Commander (Sundial): continuity/surge/conflicts; approve coverage-reducing/nonstandard exceptions; review staging coverage; escalate jurisdictionally, respect clinical authority; send Mutual Aid Release Form releasing neighboring service. Radio Coordinator (Mistral): verify talkgroups/reachability/backups; transmit assignments/hazards through Regional Radio Network; retry missing acknowledgments/escalate; send Coverage Gap Bulletin; confirm route changes. Handoff requires crew acknowledgment/dispatch confirmation. Paramedic Crew: protocol/scope care; repeat location/priority; report clinical/readiness/status/barrier changes, unsuitable routes. Ambulance Unit 417: report staging position/status; await confirmed relocation/response. Fleet Maintenance Cell (Bluejay): defects/restrictions/clearance; Battery Swap Voucher authorizes replacement. Hospital Liaison Desk (Kestrel): capacity/compatibility; coordinate destination consultation using condition/transport estimate/acceptance; confirm Emergency Department acceptance; record outcomes/send restrictions to Juniper. Emergency Department reports capacity/access/status; Bedside Arrival Receipt confirms arrival. Riverside Trauma Center: suitability/availability/guidance.

New part:
S159: The Radio Coordinator relays destination instructions to the Paramedic Crew over the Regional Radio Network.
S160: The Paramedic Crew acknowledges the destination and advises dispatch if conditions require renewed consultation.
S161: The South Gate Status Board produces the South Access Lane Notice when the south approach has a material access constraint.
S162: The South Gate Status Board displays current access information for crews approaching the receiving facility through the south entrance.
S163: The Shift Commander reviews access constraints that could affect arrival timing or safe patient transfer.
S164: The Regional Radio Network supports updates between dispatch and the Paramedic Crew while the ambulance is en route.
S165: Call Taker Mara receives the Bedside Arrival Receipt to support completion of the incident record.
S166: Call Taker Mara verifies that the recorded arrival time is consistent with the dispatch timeline and crew communications.
S167: Ambulance Unit 417 reports arrival at the receiving facility and confirms when patient handover is complete.
S168: The Emergency Department and the Paramedic Crew clarify any discrepancy in patient identity or transfer documentation before the crew clears the facility.
S169: The Data Quality Officer reviews incomplete arrival or handover fields during routine record-quality checks.
S170: The Regional Dispatch Center updates the incident status after receiving confirmation that the patient has been transferred to facility care.
S171: The Hospital Liaison Desk remains available to resolve facility-level questions that arise during or immediately after handover.
S172: The Shift Commander escalates unresolved destination or access issues through established regional coordination procedures.
S173: Surge operations begin when queue age, simultaneous high-priority calls, or staffed unit availability crosses thresholds approved by regional policy.
S174: Regional Dispatch Center monitors these indicators continuously and declares the applicable surge level when a threshold is met.
S175: Computer Aided Dispatch Console displays the current surge level and the operational constraints reported by field and facility staff.
S176: Triage Supervisor validates the declaration and confirms that call prioritization remains consistent with clinical protocols.
S177: Shift Commander assigns coordination responsibilities and reviews whether normal coverage can be maintained during the surge.
S178: Regional Medical Director provides clinical direction when demand exceeds routine triage guidance or requires a regional protocol adjustment.
S179: Hospital Liaison Desk uses the Pediatric Acuity Note to convey pediatric monitoring and destination considerations to receiving staff.
S180: Pediatric calls with concerning airway, breathing, circulation, or mental status findings receive prompt clinical escalation under approved protocols.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
